Domain and email Every plan includes a free domain for the first year. Premium comes with 2 mailboxes per website, free for one year, and Unlimited and Cloud Startup with unlimited mailboxes. Treat those as individual experiences, not averages. Our Hostinger customer support guide shows how to get from the AI to a human. WPBeginner states that free migration is included on all plans, and Website Planet describes a free migration tool. Who Hostinger suits and who should look elsewhere A first affiliate site or two to three niche sites: Premium. It costs $119.52 for four years, about $0.83 per site per month, if weekly backups are acceptable. Four or more sites, or frequent edits: Unlimited at $167.52. It brings daily backups, staging and 600,000 inodes. A store or growing traffic: Cloud Startup at $383.52, with 100 PHP workers and 4 CPU cores against Premium’s 40 and 1. In exchange you get phone support and daily backups on the entry plan. The full numbers are in the SiteGround vs Hostinger comparison for affiliate websites . Hostinger measured higher uptime in independent tests. The full numbers are in the Hostinger vs Namecheap comparison . Final recommendation For budget affiliate publishers, this Hostinger review ends in a clear yes: start on Premium for up to three sites, or on Unlimited if you want daily backups and staging. Read the renewal rate in your order summary before you pay, because $10.99 and $16.99 a month apply after 48 months. Skip it if you need a phone line or cannot prepay four years. If the refunded plan included a free domain, its standard price may be deducted. Domain renewals and most country-code domains are not refundable, and .com, .net and .org domains only within 96 hours of registration. Hostinger’s pricing page lists the domain as free for one year. WPBeginner notes that it renews at the regular price after that. Is Hostinger good for a busy WooCommerce store? TechRadar says it does not have the power for the most demanding websites, and WPBeginner suggests a different host for high-traffic stores. For a small store, Cloud Startup’s 100 PHP workers give more room than Premium’s 40.

text: Hostinger is the cheapest credible shared host on the market, and the discount is real. So is the renewal. Understanding how the two relate is most of what you need to decide whether it fits. What the price actually is Hostinger's headline rate assumes a four-year prepayment. From its own pricing page: Plan 48-month total Effective monthly Renews at Increase Entry $143.52 $2.99/mo $10.99/mo ×3.7 Mid $181.92 $3.79/mo $16.99/mo ×4.5 Upper $383.52 $7.99/mo $25.99/mo ×3.3 Two things follow. The $2.99 requires paying $143.52 up front for four years. On a twelve-month term the effective rate is meaningfully higher. The advertised figure is the best case, not the default. Renewal is three to four and a half times the intro rate. That is steeper than most of the market. A mid plan bought at $3.79 renews at $16.99 — more than a comparable plan costs at hosts whose intro pricing looked worse. This is not a hidden cost; Hostinger publishes it. It is a structural feature of the offer: heavily discounted acquisition, full-rate retention. Decide against $10.99–$25.99, and treat the first four years as a discount you happen to get. What you get for it LiteSpeed. Hostinger runs LiteSpeed rather than Apache, with LSCache available for WordPress. For a cached WordPress site this is a genuine performance advantage over a stock Apache stack, and it is the main technical reason Hostinger benchmarks well for the price. hPanel. Its own control panel rather than cPanel — one of the responses to cPanel's per-account licensing. Clean, well organised, and easier for a beginner than cPanel. It is also proprietary, so the familiarity does not travel. Global datacentres. More location choice than most budget hosts, which matters for latency. Free domain and SSL on longer terms. Real value, though the domain renews at market rate. Where it stops working Resource limits arrive before you expect them. Shared hosting allocates CPU and I/O per account, and Hostinger's entry tiers are tight. A site that grows into real traffic will hit throttling rather than a hard failure — slower responses at peak, which is harder to diagnose than an outage. No root, no arbitrary services. Standard for shared hosting, and worth stating: if you need a background worker, a non-standard runtime or a custom daemon, you have outgrown the product. Support is broad rather than deep. Fine for panel questions and routine problems. Less useful for anything requiring someone to reason about your specific stack. Who it fits A good fit if you are running one or several small-to-medium WordPress sites, you value price highly, and you are willing to prepay to get the rate. For a first site, a portfolio, a small business brochure site or a blog that is not yet a business, it is hard to beat. A poor fit if your site is load-bearing for revenue and growing. The point at which shared hosting stops being adequate arrives sooner than most people plan for, and the migration is easier before it becomes urgent. Managed VPS versus shared hosting covers where that line sits. Verdict The best value in shared hosting on a four-year term, and a fairly ordinary deal at renewal. LiteSpeed is a real advantage at this price point. hPanel is genuinely good and genuinely proprietary. Buy it for what it is: cheap, capable hosting for small sites, on a discount that expires. Do not buy it expecting the entry price to be the ongoing price, and do not buy it for a site you expect to grow into serious traffic. Frequently asked questions Is Hostinger really $2.99 a month? On a 48-month prepayment, yes — $143.52 up front. On shorter terms the effective rate is higher, and it renews at $10.99. Is Hostinger fast? For cached WordPress on LiteSpeed, yes, and unusually so for the price. Under sustained traffic on an entry plan you will meet the resource limits before you meet the server's limits. Is hPanel as good as cPanel? For most tasks, better — cleaner and easier to learn. The trade is portability: hPanel only exists at Hostinger. The same argument applies to SPanel at ScalaHosting . Can I run a shop on it? A small one, yes. As order volume and catalogue size grow, the resource limits become the constraint. Plan the move before conversion rates start reflecting response times. What happens at renewal? You pay the published renewal rate. Hostinger states it clearly at purchase; the mistake is budgeting from the promotional figure. I set up an identical WordPress site with a default theme and test content, including images, on a custom domain with no caching plugins. Then I ran the same four tests – GTmetrix for speed and LCP, k6 for stress with 50 virtual users at the same time, a response-time test from 6 global regions, and 30 days of UptimeRobot monitoring. Those four tests make up the performance side of the WPBeginner Score, which counts for 80% of the total. Each test carries a set weight, so no single lucky number can carry a host. The other 20% of the score comes from value. For that part I look at what the plan really costs and gives you in return – the intro price, the renewal price, how many sites and how much storage you get, the plan limits, and the quality of support. The full methodology, the exact weights, and every host’s raw numbers are in our best WordPress hosting guide. Hostinger Performance Test Results Below you can find my full Hostinger speed test results. Speed Test – 659 ms LCP Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures how quickly the main content of a page appears. It is the speed number Google’s Core Web Vitals care about most. My Hostinger test site showed an LCP of 659 ms, and the full page finished loading in 1.1 seconds. That result beats similarly priced hosts like Bluehost (933 ms) and DreamHost (986 ms) on the same test. The fastest host in our comparison, Levamo , loaded in 358 ms, but it costs about ten times more per month. For a $2.69 shared hosting plan with no caching plugins installed, this is a strong speed result. Server Response Time – 227 ms Global Average Speed test tools load the whole page with images included, but that’s only one part of the performance. To see raw server speed, I also measured time to first byte (TTFB) from data centers in 6 regions around the world. Hostinger averaged 227 ms across the 6 regions. That was the best average response time of all the hosts we tested. Response times stayed strong across North America, Europe, and Asia. South America was the slowest region at a 440 ms TTFB, which is still quicker than the global averages of several hosts in our comparison. If your audience is spread around the world, a CDN will serve your content from locations closer to your visitors. Hostinger includes its CDN on the Business plan and higher, so factor that into your plan choice. Stress Test – 21 ms P95 Under Load To see how a host behaves under a traffic spike, I sent 50 virtual users to the test site with k6 by Grafana Labs and recorded the P95 response time. Hostinger held a 21 ms P95 response time with no failed requests. Its LiteSpeed cache kicked in immediately and kept response times flat as the traffic climbed. This was one of the strongest under-load results in our comparison. It means a growing blog or a small online store on Hostinger can absorb a sudden traffic spike without slowing down. Uptime – 100% Over 30 Days I monitored the Hostinger test site with UptimeRobot, checking every 5 minutes. Over the 30-day window, it recorded 100% uptime with no incidents. Hostinger backs its hosting with a 99.9% uptime guarantee, and in our monitoring window, it stayed above its own promise. That result matches my long-term experience with my own sites there, which have never faced downtime that needed my attention. How Hostinger Compares to Other Hosts We Tested The speed test numbers on their own do not give you the full picture. Here is how Hostinger performed compared to other similarly priced hosts from our comparison, all tested with the identical setup. Hostinger’s 88 reflects exactly what you see above. It leads this group on response time, beats most of it on speed, and packs more tools into its entry plan than most hosts at this price. To see the full rankings, and the raw data for every host we tested, check out our best WordPress hosting guide. Hostinger’s Infrastructure and Technology Most other Hostinger reviews skip what’s under the hood on their shared hosting platform, but I believe it’s worth highlighting. Caching and speed – Hostinger’s shared plans run LiteSpeed caching, which is the layer that kept our stress test at a 21 ms response. Hostinger also lists one-click object caching among its WordPress optimization features. Control panel – instead of cPanel, Hostinger built its own control panel called hPanel. It covers the same jobs, including WordPress installs, email, databases, a PHP version manager, and a drag-and-drop file manager. Data centers – Hostinger runs servers in the USA, Europe (France, Germany, the Netherlands, Lithuania, and the United Kingdom), Asia (Indonesia and Singapore), and South America (Brazil). CDN and security – every plan gets a free SSL certificate, DDoS protection, and Cloudflare-protected nameservers, and the CDN comes with the Business plan and higher. Developers also get Git access on shared plans. File limits – hosting providers often cap the number of files your account can hold, and that cap is usually the first thing a growing site hits. Hostinger allows 400,000 files on the Premium plan and up to 2 million on its entry cloud plan, so a media-heavy site can stay on a cheap plan for years. Hostinger Hosting Plans and Pricing Hostinger offers shared, cloud, VPS, and eCommerce hosting, plus a website builder. For most readers of this review, the shared WordPress plans are the relevant ones. Premium – 3 websites, 20 GB SSD storage, weekly backups, a free domain for the first year, and 2 free email mailboxes per site for the first year. $2.69 per month with our link on a 48-month term, renews at $10.99 per month. The CDN, AI tools, and priority support are not included at this level – they start on the Business plan. Business – unlimited websites and mailboxes, 50 GB NVMe storage, daily backups with easy restore, the CDN, integrated eCommerce tools, AI tools, and priority support. $3.41 per month with our link on a 48-month term, renews at $16.99 per month. Cloud Startup – built for bigger sites and agencies, with 100 GB NVMe storage and daily and on-demand backups. $7.19 per month on a 48-month term, renews at $25.99 per month. All plans include hPanel, a free SSL certificate, 1-click WordPress installation, free website migration, and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Hostinger does not recommend the Premium plan for eCommerce stores with more than ten products. In my experience, a new blog or small business site will not outgrow Premium for a long time. You can move to the Business plan when you need the CDN, the AI tools, daily backups, or more than 3 websites. Look at Cloud Startup when your store or your traffic starts to grow. Free and Paid Hosting Addons Hostinger’s headline price is honest, but a few extras follow first-year rules. Knowing these up front will save you surprise charges. Free domain – free for the first year on the shared plans, then it renews at the regular domain price. If you cancel within the 30-day guarantee window, the refund does not include domain registration fees, but you get to keep your domain. This is fairly standard practice across shared hosts that offer a free domain. Email mailboxes – each website gets 2 free mailboxes for the first year. After year one, keeping them becomes a paid add-on, which is also common across budget hosts. Backups – Premium includes weekly backups, and daily backups start on the Business plan. I recommend you set up your own backup solution regardless of your hosting provider’s backup policy. Refund rules – the money-back guarantee covers your hosting fees and runs for the first 30 days after signup. Add-ons like domain registration are excluded. Hostinger for WordPress Beginners Hostinger makes starting out easy. The 1-click WordPress installer sets up your site in minutes, and hPanel keeps your websites, domains, email, and security in one clean place. The AI toolkit goes further than what most budget hosts offer, though the site-building AI tools start on the Business plan. Every customer gets Kodee, an AI assistant that can troubleshoot common WordPress issues. I was not expecting much from Kodee at first. But a few times when I ran into minor hosting issues, it solved my problem without me needing to wait for a human agent. I would treat the AI tools as a convenience rather than a reason to choose a host. For a first-timer, though, they remove real friction. Hostinger Customer Support Hostinger offers 24/7 support over live chat and email, plus a large knowledge base with step-by-step tutorials. Priority response comes with the Business plan and higher, and there is no phone support on any plan. Kodee, the AI assistant, is your first touch point, and it handles most common questions instantly. You can ask for a human agent at any time, and in my experience the team responds quickly. If you purchased your hosting through one of Hostinger’s local websites, such as hostinger.in, you can also get support in that local language. To be fair, phone support is rare at budget hosting prices, and most hosts at this level stick to chat. Bluehost adds phone on its Business plan or higher, and of all the budget hosts that we tested, SiteGround was one of the few that included phone support on every plan. Who Should Use Hostinger and Who Should Look Elsewhere Choose Hostinger if you want the best overall mix of speed, tools, and price for a new WordPress website. Its 88 WPBeginner Score and its strong showing across all four of our tests make it the pick I recommend to most people. Its 100% uptime in our monitoring backs the reliability claim. Look elsewhere if you need phone support, since SiteGround includes it on every plan. The same goes if you want to run many websites on one cheap plan (Bluehost includes 10 on its entry plan), or you run a high-traffic eCommerce site that needs managed hosting under load, where Levamo is our pick (see our full hosting comparison ). Final Verdict – Is Hostinger the Right Choice for You? Hostinger is the best overall WordPress host I tested this year. It pairs strong speed test results with more included tools than most similarly priced plans, and my own sites have run on it without trouble for more than 5 years. My verdict – if you are starting a WordPress website and want the best overall value, visit Hostinger and start on the Premium plan. If you need phone support or run a high-traffic store, our best WordPress hosting comparison shows which host won each category on the same tests. FAQs About Hostinger 1. What are the disadvantages of Hostinger? Based on our tests and plan research, the main ones are the entry plan limits (3 websites and 20 GB storage, where some hosts give you more), the 48-month term required for the $2.69 price, the $10.99 per month renewal, and no phone support. Performance was not one of them, since Hostinger posted some of the strongest numbers in our comparison. 2. Is Hostinger good for beginners? Yes. Hostinger installs WordPress in one click, hPanel is one of the clearest control panels I have used, and the Kodee AI assistant answers common questions instantly. The AI website builder and 24/7 chat support round it out. It is our best overall pick for someone starting a new WordPress site. 3. Can Hostinger handle high traffic? In our stress test, Hostinger held a 21 ms P95 response with 50 concurrent users and no failed requests, thanks to its LiteSpeed cache. That was one of the strongest under-load results we recorded. For consistently high-traffic or eCommerce sites, a managed host like Levamo is still the safer long-term pick. Hostinger’s own cloud and VPS plans are also an easy upgrade path. 4. Is Hostinger better than Bluehost? On our identical tests, Hostinger was faster. It loaded with a 659 ms LCP against Bluehost’s 933 ms, and its 227 ms global response beat Bluehost’s 599 ms. Bluehost counters with 10 websites on its entry plan, where Hostinger includes 3, and the simplest setup for a first site. Our Hostinger vs Bluehost comparison goes deeper. 5. Why is Hostinger so cheap? Hostinger keeps prices low by limiting server resources on each plan and by asking for a longer term upfront for the best rate. Once your website grows and hits a resource limit, you can upgrade to their cloud or VPS plans. 6. Where are Hostinger’s servers located? Hostinger’s headquarters are in Kaunas, Lithuania. Its servers run in the USA, Europe (France, Germany, the Netherlands, Lithuania, and the United Kingdom), Asia (Indonesia and Singapore), and South America (Brazil). That global spread showed in our response time test, where Hostinger averaged 227 ms across 6 regions. 7. Does Hostinger offer a free domain name? Yes, Hostinger includes a free domain name for the first year with its shared hosting plans. After the first year, the domain renews at the regular registration price, which is standard across hosting companies. 8. Which Hostinger plan should I get? We recommend starting with their Premium plan . It covers 3 websites and includes a free domain, which is more than a new site needs. Upgrading later takes a few clicks, so there is no reason to overbuy on day one. So, I figured I shouldn’t expect much in the way of performance or features for a service that doesn’t require me to sell both kidneys to pay for it. Of course the top-tiered Cloud Startup plan would be impressive. Most providers love to focus their standout features on the most outrageously-priced plan. Optimized Performance From LiteSpeed Web Server New WordPress sites are pre-optimized for maximum speed with Hostinger Hostinger uses the impressively fast LiteSpeed web server – this is the software running on the physical server that delivers your website’s content to your visitors. LiteSpeed outperforms the more traditional Apache web server, upon which many other web hosts still rely due to its open-source (i.e. free) license. LiteSpeed itself already offers great performance, but its LiteSpeed Cache for WordPress plugin stores pre-loaded (cached) copies of your web pages , which can then be more quickly delivered to your visitors. Additionally, Hostinger uses MariaDB rather than MySQL for Web and Cloud plans, offering faster performance overall. Also, since Hostinger pre-configures LiteSpeed based on your needs, you won’t have to worry about a complicated installation process reserved only for the technically-inclined. Object caching and WordPress staging options are built directly into Hostinger’s panel, which allows you to test different configurations at the touch of a button. Discover More Hostinger Features >> Robust Security With Free SSLs and Automatic Backups Hostinger gives you plenty of control over your backups Data loss can be absolutely ruinous for an online business. Fortunately, Hostinger understands the importance of security and provides protection from an array of potential disasters and online threats. With Hostinger’s Secure Access Manager, you can assign specific roles and permissions to collaborators , which is ideal for developers or teams managing multiple projects. In addition, the AI Security Audit scans for suspicious bot activity and access anomalies, helping safeguard your SEO and site performance. Every Hostinger plan includes all the essentials : free SSL, an in-house web application firewall (WAF), an automatic malware scanner, and Cloudflare DDoS protection for its nameservers – not to be confused with Cloudflare’s content delivery network (CDN), which isn’t enabled by default. While its security suite isn’t the most advanced, it still protects against the most common threats, and it’s more than you’ll get from most budget hosts. Connecting a Domain and Installing WordPress Once your account has been created, Hostinger takes you through some setup steps. I was first presented with a short questionnaire to help me set up the hosting environment. This is where I also auto-configured LiteSpeed’s caching to maximize performance based on my particular needs. This allowed me to take full advantage of LiteSpeed without having to figure out how to optimize the settings myself. From there, I was asked if I would like to install WordPress automatically . Overall, Hostinger sets up nearly all of the hosting and basic WordPress framework for you. For those who want more advanced control, Hostinger’s cloud plans also include WP-CLI and SSH access so you can install your own software manually, as well as full root access on VPS plans. 4.9 Performance One of the Fastest Budget Web Hosts Out There Hostinger consistently delivers performance that rivals far pricier providers. In my hands-on testing, following our performance testing process , it proved to be one of the fastest shared hosts I have used , easily outperforming top competitors like IONOS, SiteGround, and HostArmada. Hostinger’s infrastructure runs on LiteSpeed Web Server with NVMe SSD storage and built-in server-level caching, helping websites load quickly even under heavy traffic. With data centers across the US, Europe, Asia, and South America, Hostinger lets you host your website closer to your target audience for faster loading times . Higher-tier plans also include access to a built-in CDN, which stores cached versions of your site on global servers. This ensures that visitors get consistently fast load speeds, even if they’re far from your chosen data center. Our custom test site has all the typical elements of an e-commerce site To test Hostinger fairly, we built a website to simulate an average landing page filled with text, high-quality images, custom fonts, and plenty of complex code for interactive elements . I then monitored this website using multiple testing tools – namely GTmetrix, Sucuri Load Time Tester, and UptimeRobot. Our test site with Hostinger achieved a typical loading time of about 0.8s and 100% uptime over a month. Put simply, it would be difficult to find better performance than this at Hostinger’s prices – see the impressive results for yourself below. GTmetrix I used GTmetrix to test our website’s performance in a local setting . To do this, I selected a source server in the US, not too far away from my test site’s data center. I then completed a week-long performance analysis with hourly speed tests. GTmetrix gave Hostinger an A rating So, what did I find? During a week of testing, my website on Hostinger’s server achieved a typical Fully Loaded Time of just 0.8s . To put that in perspective, most other budget hosts hover around 2s to 3s – Hostinger manages to be several times faster. How does it do this? Well, it is due in part to the default LiteSpeed optimization settings enabled by Hostinger when I first installed WordPress. For example, the default image compression reduced the total content on my test page in size from about 1 MB to just under 800 KB , allowing the page to load more quickly. Besides a few hiccups, Hostinger’s performance was consistent There were a few instances where my site took 1.5s to 2.0s to load. However, even these worst-case results are still within acceptable guidelines for visitor retention. And notably, as each of our tests is conducted from a “fresh” browser instance, some of the cache settings don’t affect these results – but a real website visitor should see the page load even faster on repeat visits . The results for Time to First Byte – the amount of time it takes for the server to start sending website data – were typically around 0.2s. This is a very good speed – it isn’t unusual to see this number at 0.5s or higher from shared hosting services. Sucuri Load Time Tester Next, I wanted to take a look at how Hostinger performed on a global scale . To do this, I used Sucuri’s Load Time Tester. Hostinger offers data centers located in the US, Europe, Asia, and South America. If your website is aimed at attracting visitors from Africa, Australia, or the Middle East, it’s advisable to select the closest accessible data center to their respective locations to get the best loading speeds. To get the best loading speeds on an international scale, you’ll usually need to have a CDN (content delivery network) active. This saves copies of your website’s content (images and code, for example) on servers around the world, so visitors far away from your chosen data center can access some of your content from a server that is closer to them. Most providers do not have a CDN pre-enabled, requiring you to set one up yourself. While Hostinger supports Cloudflare’s CDN, you’ll have to sign up for an account and configure it yourself, even if you’re just using the free Cloudflare plan. Because we test hosting plans “out of the box” in their default state so we can tell you how well they will work for beginner users , I didn’t enable Cloudflare’s CDN. With a CDN, Hostinger would perform better globally, but these results are pretty good The results were surprising. My test site achieved loading speeds of about 1s in Europe and South America, despite being hosted at one of Hostinger’s US data centers . While it was far slower in Singapore and Australia, reaching around 2s, this is still well within acceptable limits. In fact, these results are better than some of the budget hosts in these regions can deliver on their own home turf. UptimeRobot Finally, I measured Hostinger’s reliability. After all, it doesn’t matter how fast a host can make your website load if it’s rarely online to begin with. To test Hostinger’s uptime, I monitored our test website with UptimeRobot for an entire month . Whenever an instance of downtime occurred, it would be recorded. It really doesn’t get better than this – well done, Hostinger Amazingly, there were no instances of downtime to record . Our test site was online and available for the duration of the testing period. Thankfully, by my tests, it doesn’t look like you’ll frequently need to claim compensation, if ever. 4.7 Support Support Is Polite but Primarily Relies on Links to Documentation Hostinger provides 24/7 customer support through live chat and email, though there’s no phone option available. So, yeah… I wouldn’t put all of my faith in Kodee for complex queries (just yet), but this AI assistant is definitely a helpful first line of support that’s quicker and faster to access than an agent. Overall, Hostinger’s support system is built for efficiency rather than hands-on guidance. The knowledge base handles most setup and troubleshooting questions, making it the quickest option. Live chat is best for account or technical issues, while email works well for detailed inquiries. And while Kodee is useful for quick answers, it can’t replace Hostinger’s experts.
